Babchyntsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Babchyntsi's Jewish community, settled in the mid-18th century, grew tobacco and traded goods before Russia's 1882 'May Laws' stripped Jews of the right to lease land for plantations, significantly damaging the community's finances. Its synagogue was repurposed as a four-year Yiddish school in the 1920s before later being demolished. In August 1941, 94 of the town's 192 Jews were murdered by the Nazis. This cemetery, established no later than the early 20th century, is confirmed via a local village council deputy's testimony to have lost many tombstones to construction-material theft in the 1970s and 1980s.
